body: I guess this is going to be a similar issue to #597.
I'm not sure whether or not this is backed by a HDD or not, but I can confirm that it was running without issue prior to upgrading cargo/rust.

I have the similar issue since a couple of days. Starship is getting really slow whenever I enter a folder of a project which is versionized by Git. I did not experiance any issues with older versions of starship (I'm using homebrew to keep starship up-to-date, hence I can not tell you which version worked fine). The project folder are on a MacBook Pro SSD. @samuela are your rust projects also versionized with Git? What happens when you enter normal folders (or try deleting/renaming `.git`)?

Our last libgit2 bump was on Dec 13, and that's a little long ago to be affecting this.

Is it possible that we're looking at a performance regression caused by a rustc upgrade (unlikely: my impressions were that these are pretty lightweight wrappers around libgit2)? Or perhaps a performance regression in libgit2 itself?
Not sure is Rust related, got same issue with an Elixir repo, I think is related to Git
Yes this rust project is git version controlled. I tested on a git non-rust folder and that didn't seem to have any issues.
Is the repo open source so I can clone it to try and reproduce the problem? 😄

> Is the repo open source so I can clone it to try and reproduce the problem? 😄

It doesn't seem like this repo is anomalous. Any large repo will do. My go-to choice for a large repo is https://github.com/chromium/chromium. If you can make prompt fast while in that repo, it'll be fast for the vast majority of all users.
I had a go on the Linux repo and it's noticeably slower, but not as extreme as 20 seconds.

> I had a go on the Linux repo and it's noticeably slower, but not as extreme as 20 seconds.

chromium is over 10x the size of linux repo.

That should hopefully make the problem easier to spot, thanks. Cloning it now. 😄 

In the meantime, here's a flamegraph from the Linux repo, which does show where most of the time has gone:

```
cargo flamegraph --freq 1000000 --bin=starship -- prompt -p ../../linux
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/338027/74108201-a894d280-4b6f-11ea-9c4b-fe69c195695f.png)

> In the meantime, here's a flamegraph from the Linux repo, which does show where most of the time has gone:

This basically shows libgit2, as expected.

At this point it's common knowledge that fetching git status with libgit2 is slow. See https://github.com/libgit2/libgit2/issues/4230.
In my case the repo is https://github.com/samuela/rustybox

> In my case the repo is https://github.com/samuela/rustybox

Interesting. This is a small repo. On my machine `lg2 status` takes 4.8 milliseconds in rustybox. This command approximates what starship is doing.

In a clean Git repo `lg2 status` takes time proportional to the number of files in the index. This repository has 1289 files -- a relatively small number.

`lg2 status` can get much slower if the repository isn't clean. There are many potential bottlenecks here and which one you hit depends on how exactly the repository is unclean.

@samuela Do you experience high starship latency in a clean rustybox repository? If so, could you run the following command either from bash or zsh while in a clean rustybox repo and post its output?

```zsh
time ( for i in {1..100}; do git status; done ) >/dev/null
```

I just tried again today, and now it seems to be back to normal... Maybe it was some sort of transient issue on the machine. FWIW I'm running this in Docker on a machine running CentOS 7 that I don't manage but doesn't really have any other users.

```
❯ time ( for i in {1..100}; do git status; done ) >/dev/null
( for i in {1..100}; do; git status; done; ) > /dev/null  0.39s user 0.96s system 121% cpu 1.116 total
```

Also in my case `git status` ran without a hitch even when starship was taking forever. So I'm guessing that it's not directly related to the size of the repo.

I just came across a similar issue on my local Macbook Pro. The starship prompt takes 7 seconds in a clone of https://gitlab.redox-os.org/redox-os/redox. Here's a screencast: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rf7nMjv7Z-Q
Same issue, anywhere from 10 to 20 second wait inside large git repos.
I am wondering if it is possible to add options to use default git instead of libgit2, which can do some tunnings like config watchman as `core.fsmonitor` ...
@samuela git has an untracked file cache (which also supports using watchman to invalidate) which libgit does not have, so the amount of ignored and untracked files is another factor.
@krisselden That could be the problem but IIRC I don't have that many untracked files in this repo.
@samuela try deleting your target folder, see if that changes it.  Another thing to try is `git gc --aggressive --prune`.
I think this was directly after a clone, so I don't think I had any compiled artifacts.

I'm experiencing this as well; I'm not sure when it started happening. Hitting enter in a large repo takes seconds to get to a new prompt. It's clearly git that's the issue, not Rust, so maybe this issue can be renamed.

Just as I stated in https://github.com/starship/starship/issues/597#issuecomment-646984646 , this is a known issue for starship members for a long time. And matchai has been working on this feature and has gotten a fairly good result in https://github.com/matchai/starship-poc . So keep your eyes on :)
The v0.46.2 release should have improved git status performance by about 2x. We're still working on improvements 👍

Similar to #940 I am going to close this issue since we have switched to calling git and parsing the output rather than using libgit2. As mentioned in the other issue this should both be faster for larger repos and will respect the `command_timeout` setting so starship won't hang while trying to get the status of the repo. While this isn't a perfect solution it should hopefully be sufficient until we can introduce a cache, async rendering, a daemon or some combination of all three.
